1.explanation:
1. We add a `readOnly` boolean control in the story so we can toggle it on/off in Storybook.
2. We pass `readOnly` to the outer `<TimePicker>` as well as both `<TimePickerSelect>` children. This aligns with how TextInput implements read-only states.
3. In the Jest test, we verify the top-level container gets the `bx--time-picker--readonly` class when `readOnly` is true.
4. With this code, you can run Storybook and flip the `ReadOnly` story to see the gray backgrounds, disabled icons, and no text caret exactly as the design mockups require.
1.bug_scenario: In the Carbon React TimePicker component, there is no “read-only” styling or class applied when you pass a readOnly prop. In the designs, a read-only time picker appears with a gray background on its text input and selects, and the caret is removed. The screenshot in the bug report shows exactly how the hh:mm field and the two dropdowns should look when read-only (same spacing, same disabled icon color, same container background), but the current implementation ignores the readOnly prop entirely.
